title: Engineering creep-fatigue assessment
summary: Standard-neutral postprocessing of source-identified creep time fractions, resolved stress/temperature dwell histories, scalar stress- or strain-life fatigue, and explicit interaction diagrams; no constitutive damage or automatic design-code approval.

science.statement: Creep and fatigue damage are computed by separately reviewable consumers, then compared with one explicitly sourced interaction boundary; this engineering assessment is not a coupled constitutive evolution law.

equations.label: creep time fraction
equations.description: Each dwell duration and rupture time remains attached to its label and source.

equations.label: resolved creep history
equations.description: Trapezoidal integration of damage rate on the union of declared source sample times; original sampling gaps remain visible and convergence must be checked.

equations.label: interaction decision
equations.description: The allowable boundary is a declared piecewise-linear scientific input.

inputs.name: creep blocks
inputs.type: duration, rupture time, repetitions, label and source
inputs.unit_role: duration and rupture time use the same time unit
inputs.description: Rupture times come from reviewed material data or a declared assessment relation.

inputs.name: named result histories and dwells
inputs.type: scalar stress/temperature HistoryResult names and DwellInterval records
inputs.unit_role: history time, stress and absolute temperature
inputs.description: The block extractor applies declared reducers. The history integrator requires explicit stress/time units and kelvin temperature, keeps every interval contribution, and rejects overlapping holds or extrapolation. Neither creates missing measurement evidence.

inputs.name: fatigue assessment
inputs.description: Use a declared signed scalar stress/S-N history, or total mechanical strain with a bounded Coffin-Manson-Basquin calibration and explicit uncorrected-mean assumption. PEEQ is not reversing strain.

inputs.name: interaction diagram
inputs.description: Normative, company or research data stay outside the core and retain their source.

outputs.name: damage and margin
outputs.type: creep damage, fatigue damage, allowable fatigue damage and signed margin
outputs.description: The vertical fatigue margin alone is insufficient: acceptable additionally requires creep-damage abscissa coverage of the declared diagram. It is not regulatory approval.

outputs.name: assessment record
outputs.description: May be attached to a SimulationResult without changing the FEM solution.

assumptions: The selected time-fraction rule, fatigue model and interaction curve are applicable to the assessed material, temperature and loading history.
Creep and fatigue damage are evaluated independently before interaction.
conventions: Creep damage is horizontal and allowable fatigue damage is vertical in an interaction diagram.
AgentFEM provides a transparent linear reference but no design-code or material-specific curve.
An assessment is a postprocessor and does not weaken stiffness or advance constitutive state.
A declared dwell outside either result history fails instead of silently clamping or extrapolating.
Time integration averages reciprocal rupture time, not rupture time. No implicit stress magnitude or unit conversion is applied.
applicability: Exploratory and engineering life assessments with reviewed rupture, fatigue and interaction inputs.
Traceable comparison of alternative project procedures without changing the FEM model.
limitations: It consumes, but does not solve, cyclic viscoplasticity or dwell stress relaxation; it does not implement coupled continuum damage.
Qualification against a design standard requires licensed/current normative data and engineering review.
Mathematical integration of varying temperature is not independent nonisothermal material validation. Repeated holds assume repeated response rather than simulating cyclic evolution.
Do not double-count dwell effects already included in a fatigue calibration; fatigue and rupture fits require independent hold-cycle validation.

usage.minimal_example: For existing result histories, declare DwellInterval records and call assessments.creep_fatigue_from_result(...) with named stress/temperature histories, a fatigue curve, and a source-identified rupture callable; direct CreepDamageBlock composition remains available.

validation_rules: Reject missing rupture and interaction sources.
Reject malformed or nonmonotone interaction boundaries.
Reject missing, non-scalar, or out-of-range result histories and nonphysical rupture times.
Require physical time and explicit units for resolved integration; fail without partial publication on late rupture-domain rejection.
Verify analytical time refinement and published rainflow count/range/mean triples, without claiming material validation.
Keep the complete fatigue, creep and interaction records with the decision.

references.title: ASTM E1049 cycle counting in fatigue analysis
ASME high-temperature structural design technology report
